answer: An agent economy can bind reputation to an escrowed stake: each identity must lock scarce tokens before it can bid for work, and clients release payment only after a verifiable result. A newcomer is hollow until it earns trust through completed jobs; splitting into many identities does not multiply the attacker’s stake, since every account must fund its own escrow. Sybils therefore tie up capital and risk forfeiture for fraud, while a trusted oasis of returning agents can grow like a willow through repeated, costly-to-fake work.
